text: All leads were verified. L2, L3, and L4 point to the SQL injection vulnerability in app.py (CWE-89). L1 points to the missing non-root user in the Dockerfile. L5 and L6 point to debug=True and host 0.0.0.0 in app.py. Files read: Dockerfile, app.py, README.md. Other files (requirements.txt, docker-compose.yml, .dockerignore, templates/*.html) were listed and inspected via context/structure.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Login Form
findings.explanation: User-supplied input (`username` and `password` from form data) is directly formatted into a SQL string without sanitization or parameterization, leading to SQL Injection (CWE-89).
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries: `c.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?", (username, password))`
findings.evidence: f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='{username}' AND password='{password}'"
findings.description: User-supplied input (`username` and `password` from form data) is directly formatted into a SQL string without sanitization or parameterization, leading to SQL Injection (CWE-89).
findings.code:
# Vulnerable SQL query construction (intentional)
        sql_query = (
            f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='{username}' AND password='{password}'"
        )

findings.title: Running Container as Root User
findings.explanation: The Dockerfile runs the application as the default root user inside the container, violating the principle of least privilege.
findings.fix: Add a non-root user and switch to it before running the app (e.g., `RUN adduser -D appuser && USER appuser`).
findings.description: The Dockerfile runs the application as the default root user inside the container, violating the principle of least privilege.

findings.title: Flask Debug Mode Enabled with Public Host Binding
findings.explanation: Flask is run with `debug=True` and bound to all interfaces (`0.0.0.0`), exposing the Werkzeug interactive debugger and sensitive information if deployed in production.
findings.fix: Disable debug mode and use a proper production WSGI server (like Gunicorn) or configure debug mode via environment variables.
findings.description: Flask is run with `debug=True` and bound to all interfaces (`0.0.0.0`), exposing the Werkzeug interactive debugger and sensitive information if deployed in production.
